key_insight: A single Hamiltonian-aware reinforcement learning model can generate robust quantum control pulses across a continuous family of gate settings, learning structured solutions rather than solving each case from scratch.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, adaptable pulse synthesis for real-time quantum control, reducing reliance on repeated GRAPE re-optimization when system parameters change.
method: Model-based reinforcement learning with the Hamiltonian embedded directly into the network training loop
Single neural network outputs pulses for arbitrary rotation angles, durations, detunings, and field inhomogeneities
Learns robust control landscapes without precomputed training data
evidence_signal: On a single-spin two-level system, the trained networks produced high-fidelity pulses in milliseconds across varying parameters, with fidelities comparable to multi-seed GRAPE.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on a simple two-level system, so scaling to larger, noise-rich quantum hardware may require careful validation and retraining.
paper_title: Uncovering Latent Structures in Robust Pulse Sequences: A Model-Based Reinforcement Learning Approach for Adaptable Quantum Control
